English · A1+ · Final class

My Family

Fundamental 1 — Class 15. Review the basics, become a family detective, and finish the level by describing people who matter to you.

⏱ Suggested duration: 120 minutesSession 1 of 6🎯 Goal: Describe a family clearly
Today’s mission: use simple English to talk about family members, ages, jobs, appearance, personality and likes. You may describe your real family, a chosen family, or an imaginary family.

1. Quick-Fire Challenge ⚡

10 minutes · Fast answers · No multiple choice

How to play

Each challenge gives a picture clue, description, calculation, or spoken prompt—not the answer. Students respond aloud as quickly as they can. You decide if the answer is correct, and give a point to the student or team. No options and no automatic scoring!

SPELLING ✍️Challenge 1 of 20
Spell the word: FAMILY.

Look at the clue or listen carefully. Answer aloud—your teacher is the referee! 🧑‍⚖️

✍️ Spelling

Use a picture clue or listen to a name, then spell it without seeing the word.

🔢 Numbers

Solve a quick calculation, work out an age, or repeat digits you hear.

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Family & English

Use relationship clues, describe a person, or correct a sentence.

Teacher tip 💡 Keep the pace lively: give about 5–10 seconds per challenge. Accept answers orally, ask students to spell aloud when needed, and invite the class to help after an attempt.
➡️ Transition from the review: “Great work! You have refreshed some important English from Fundamental 1. Now let’s use that language for a real purpose: talking about people and family relationships.”

2. Meet My Family

15 minutes · Read the model, notice the language, then check your understanding.

Model poster

A simple family description

This is my family. We are four people and a dog.

My dad is 42 years old. He is tall and has short, dark hair. He works in an office. He is kind and funny.

My mom is 40 years old. She is medium height and has long, dark hair. She is a teacher. She is patient and loving.

My brother is 16 years old. He is tall and has curly hair. He is a student. He likes sports and video games.

My sister is 12 years old. She is short and has long, straight hair. She is a student too. She loves animals and music.

And this is our dog, Max. He is friendly and very playful.

Useful language

Family

mother / mom · father / dad · brother · sister · husband · wife · son · daughter · cousin · aunt · uncle

Personal information

He is 42 years old. · She is a teacher. · They are students.

Appearance & personality

tall, short, medium height, long hair, curly hair, kind, funny, patient, friendly

Likes

He likes music. · She loves animals. · They like sports.

Reading check — 10 questions

Choose the best answer. Each answer includes an explanation.

➡️ Transition from the reading: “You have seen how a family description works. Now listen to people talking about family photos. First, focus on the general idea; then use the quiz to check details.”

3. Video 1 — Family Photo Mystery

15 minutes · Watch together, then play the comprehension game.

Before watching: Listen for family words, jobs and likes. You do not need to understand every word. First watch for the general idea; then watch again for details.

5. Sentence Builder

18 minutes · Build, complete and improve simple descriptions.

Remember: use is for identity, age and descriptions; use has for hair or features; use likes for he/she and like for I/you/we/they.

Activity A — Put the words in order

Drag-and-drop is not required: choose the correct sentence from the options.

Activity B — Complete the sentence

Activity C — Spot the mistake

➡️ Final mission: “Now it’s your turn. You have reviewed the vocabulary, read a model, listened to family conversations and practised sentence structure. Use those tools to create your own short family description.”

6. This Is My Family!

40 minutes · Plan, practise, and present.

Your mission: prepare a short description of your family. You can use the model poster, the sentence starters and your notes. Simple, clear English is the goal.

Step 1 — Plan your ideas

Step 2 — Your draft

Complete the boxes and select “Build my draft” to create a starting point. You can edit it below.

The draft is a starting point. Check names, pronouns and facts before presenting.

Step 3 — Speaking checklist

Step 4 — Present and celebrate

Speaking frame:

“Hello! This is my family. There are ___ people in my family. This is my ___. He/She is ___ years old. He/She is a ___. He/She has ___. He/She is ___ and ___. He/She likes ___. Thank you!”

Feedback for the teacher / partner

🌟 One thing you did well

“You used family words clearly.” / “Your sentences were easy to understand.” / “Great use of adjectives!”

🔧 One thing to improve

“Remember: she is 12, but she has long hair.” / “For he/she, say likes music.” / “Say my brother’s name to show possession.”
